paper_sections.title: Aging of visual word perception is related to decreased segregation within and beyond the word network in the brain
Data preprocessing for resting-state fMRI data

description.value: The study examined age-related differences in visual word perception using behavioral visual matching tasks, task-fMRI word localizer data, and resting-state seed-based functional connectivity within and beyond the word-selective network.

design.value: The study recruited healthy older and young adults, collected resting-state and task fMRI data, identified word-selective regions with a block-designed word localizer, and subsequently assessed visual form matching behavior.

description.value: The Chinese version of the Combined Raven’s Test, used to evaluate non-verbal intelligence quotient and general cognitive ability.
A visual matching task in which participants determined whether two briefly presented words were identical.
A baseline visual matching task using symbol forms to control for general cognitive aging effects.

role.value: between-subject variable and covariate controlled for in some analyses

source_definition.value: Gender was included as a covariate in between-group connectivity analyses beyond the word network.

task_description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were collected from all participants in a quiet state.
A block-designed localizer task involving a simple location judgment of Chinese characters and phase-separated Chinese characters presented to the left or right of fixation.

instructions.value: Participants judged the location of the stimulus by pressing the corresponding button as accurately and quickly as possible.

stimuli.value: Chinese characters and phase-separated Chinese characters.

task_description.value: Two visual matching tasks—word matching and symbol-form matching—using same/different trials.

instructions.value: Participants must quickly determine whether the two words on the screen are identical and press the corresponding button as swiftly and accurately as possible.

stimuli.value: 30 new pictures of words and 30 new pictures of symbols, all in stick figure style.

instrument.value: GE 3-Tesla MRI scanner (MR-750, GE Medical Systems, Milwaukee, WI)

description.value: Echo Planar Imaging (EPI) was used to obtain rs-fMRI and task-fMRI data. The imaging parameters were 43 axial slices, flip angle 90°, field of view 220 × 220 mm2, and matrix size 64 × 64. The resting session comprised 240 contiguous volumes, lasting 8 min, followed by the task localizer session, which lasted 8 min and 10 s, resulting in a continuous time course of 245 time points.

number_of_volumes.value: 240 contiguous volumes for resting-state; 245 time points in the continuous resting plus localizer time course

description.value: Task-fMRI data preprocessing included removal of the first five time points, slice timing, realignment, spatial normalization to the EPI template in Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space, and spatial smoothing using an isotropic Gaussian kernel with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 6 mm.

software.value: Data Processing and Analysis for Brain Imaging (DPABI) toolkit, based on MATLAB

steps.value: removal of the first five time points
spatial normalization to the EPI template in MNI space
spatial smoothing using an isotropic Gaussian kernel with a FWHM of 6 mm

description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were preprocessed using the DPABI toolkit, following the same procedure as a previous study.

steps.value: removal of the first 10 time points
spatial normalization to the EPI template in MNI space
regression of head motion profiles using the Friston 24-parameter model, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals

model_settings.value: The phase-scattered Chinese characters were used as a baseline; Chinese character images were contrasted against them using a linear contrast.

estimator.value: one-sample t-test for the group-level activation map

model_settings.value: Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between averaged ROI time courses or between each ROI time course and every voxel time course, followed by Fisher’s r-to-z transformation. Between-group comparisons used two-sample t-tests; gender was included as a covariate for analyses beyond the word network.

estimator.value: Pearson correlation, Fisher’s r-to-z transformation, and two-sample t-test

software.value: ppcor R package for partial correlations

model_type.value: repeated-measures analysis of variance and independent-sample t-test

model_settings.value: A 2 × 2 repeated-measures ANOVA with age group as the between-subject variable and stimulus type as the within-subject variable; an independent-sample t-test compared the IES difference between word and symbol processing.
